requirements.statement: Every category in a label is one of the 39 categories of the taxonomy, written exactly as the taxonomy writes it.

source: (text, request, material) => { const m = text.match(/"category"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/g) || []; const bad = []; const tax = null; return { ok: true, detail: 'taxonomy list not supplied in the outline; category names cannot be checked against the 39 here', spans: [] }; }
means: Each category name should match the 39-item taxonomy exactly; the taxonomy list is not in the outline, so the check cannot be completed here.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries a timecode span, start–end in mm:ss, inside the clip's duration.

source: (text, request, material) => { const spans = []; const re = /"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s*[–-]\s*(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; let m; const dm = text.match(/"duration"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/); const dur = dm ? (+dm[1])*60+(+dm[2]) : null; while ((m = re.exec(text))) { const s=(+m[1])*60+(+m[2]); const e=(+m[3])*60+(+m[4]); if (dur!==null && (e<=s || e>dur)) spans.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'span outside clip duration or end not after start'}); } return { ok: spans.length===0, detail: spans.length? spans.length+' span(s) out of range':'all spans inside duration', spans }; }
means: Each span is mm:ss–mm:ss and lies within the clip duration.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries a risk level: Low, Medium or High.

source: (text, request, material) => {
const spans = [];
let m;
const riskRe = /"risk"\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"/g;
const valid = ['Low', 'Medium', 'High'];
while ((m = riskRe.exec(text))) {
const val = m[1];
if (!valid.includes(val) && val !== 'Floor') {
spans.push({ start: m.index, end: m.index + m[0].length, why: 'risk not Low, Medium or High' });
return {
ok: spans.length === 0,
detail: spans.length ? spans.length + ' missing/invalid risk' : 'all flagged categories have a valid risk',
spans
means: Each flagged category has risk Low, Medium or High.

requirements.statement: "High" risk requires an explicit depiction in the clip: a described act, injury, blood, a weapon fired, an explicit sexual act. A reference, a mention or a discussion is Medium at most.
A clip labelled "Firearms – depiction" or "Firearms – use" is never also labelled "Floor – all brands".

source: (text, request, material) => { const hasFire=/"category"\s*:\s*"Firearms – (depiction|use)"/.test(text); const hasFloor=/"Floor – all brands"/.test(text); return { ok: !(hasFire&&hasFloor), detail: hasFire&&hasFloor?'Firearms label also carries Floor – all brands':'no conflict', spans: hasFire&&hasFloor?[{start:0,end:text.length,why:'Firearms and Floor both present'}]:[] }; }
means: A label that has a Firearms category does not also carry Floor – all brands.

requirements.statement: A clip with no flagged category is labelled "Floor – all brands" with risk Floor and no timecode.

source: (text, request, material) => { const hasCats=/"category"\s*:/.test(text); const floor=/"Floor – all brands"/.test(text); const bad=[]; if(!hasCats && !floor) bad.push({start:0,end:text.length,why:'no flagged category but not labelled Floor – all brands'}); if(!hasCats && floor && !/"risk"\s*:\s*"Floor"/.test(text)) bad.push({start:0,end:text.length,why:'Floor label without risk Floor'}); return { ok: bad.length===0, detail: bad.length? 'Floor rule broken':'Floor rule held or not applicable', spans: bad }; }
means: A clip with no flagged category is labelled Floor – all brands, risk Floor, no timecode.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries evidence: the words of the transcript, copied, that support it.

source: (text, request, material) => { const spans=[]; const re=/"category"\s*:\s*"[^"]+"[\s\S]*?"evidence"\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"/g; let m; while((m=re.exec(text))){ if(!m[1].trim()) spans.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'empty evidence'}); } return { ok: spans.length===0, detail: spans.length? spans.length+' flagged category(ies) with no evidence':'every flagged category carries evidence', spans }; }
means: Each flagged category has a non-empty evidence field; that the words are copied from the transcript is not checked here.

requirements.statement: "Violence – graphic" requires described injury or blood; a scuffle, a push or a threat is "Violence – minor".
"Language – strong" requires a word of the strong list in the transcript; "Language – mild" otherwise.
A label carries no category the transcript does not support with evidence.
Risk is the highest of the flagged categories' risk levels, carried once at the top of the label as overall.

source: (text, request, material) => { const rank={Floor:0,Low:1,Medium:2,High:3}; const ov=text.match(/"overall"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/); const risks=[...text.matchAll(/"risk"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/g)].map(x=>x[1]); if(!ov) return {ok:false,detail:'no overall',spans:[]}; if(!risks.length) return {ok:true,detail:'no flagged risks',spans:[]}; const max=risks.reduce((a,b)=>(rank[b]??0)>(rank[a]??0)?b:a, risks[0]); const ok=ov[1]===max; return { ok, detail: ok?'overall equals highest risk':'overall '+ov[1]+' but highest risk is '+max, spans: ok?[]:[{start:ov.index,end:ov.index+ov[0].length,why:'overall not highest risk'}] }; }
means: The overall field equals the highest risk among the categories.

requirements.statement: A span's end is after its start, and no span runs past the duration.

source: (text, request, material) => { const dm=text.match(/"duration"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/); const dur=dm?(+dm[1])*60+(+dm[2]):null; const spans=[]; const re=/"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s*[–-]\s*(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; let m; while((m=re.exec(text))){ const s=(+m[1])*60+(+m[2]); const e=(+m[3])*60+(+m[4]); if(e<=s||(dur!==null&&e>dur)) spans.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'end not after start or past duration'}); } return { ok: spans.length===0, detail: spans.length? spans.length+' bad span(s)':'spans ordered and within duration', spans }; }
means: Each span ends after it starts and does not exceed the duration.

requirements.statement: Where the same act is both "Violence" and "Dangerous acts", both are flagged, each with its own evidence.
A news report of a disaster is "Disaster – news", Medium at most; graphic footage described is "Disaster – graphic".
A reference to alcohol in passing is "Alcohol – reference", Low; drinking described is "Alcohol – consumption", Medium.
Numbers in a span are seconds and minutes only: no frame counts.

source: (text, request, material) => { const spans=[]; const re=/"span"\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"/g; let m; while((m=re.exec(text))){ if(/frame|\bf\d+\b|\d+\s*fps/i.test(m[1])) spans.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'frame count in span'}); } return { ok: spans.length===0, detail: spans.length? 'frame count found in span':'no frame counts in spans', spans }; }
means: Span values contain only mm:ss, with no frame counts.

requirements.statement: Evidence is copied from the transcript, never paraphrased.
A category flagged twice is listed once, with the earliest span.

source: (text, request, material) => { const seen={}; const spans=[]; const re=/"category"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/g; let m; while((m=re.exec(text))){ if(seen[m[1]]) spans.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'category listed twice'}); seen[m[1]]=true; } return { ok: spans.length===0, detail: spans.length? spans.length+' duplicate category(ies)':'each category listed once', spans }; }
means: No category name appears twice in the categories list; that the span kept is the earliest is not checked here.

requirements.statement: The label is JSON with the keys clip, duration, overall, categories; nothing else.

source: (text, request, material) => { const bad=[]; let obj; try { obj=JSON.parse(text); } catch(e) { return {ok:false,detail:'not valid JSON',spans:[{start:0,end:text.length,why:'not JSON'}]}; } const keys=Object.keys(obj).sort().join(','); const want='categories,clip,duration,overall'; const ok=keys===want; return { ok, detail: ok?'keys are clip, duration, overall, categories':'keys are '+keys, spans: ok?[]:[{start:0,end:text.length,why:'unexpected keys'}] }; }
means: The label parses as JSON and its only top-level keys are clip, duration, overall and categories.

requirements.statement: Where a clip's transcript is empty, the label is "Floor – all brands" and says so in evidence.
My pieces run 224 to 452 characters; a new piece stays between 1 and 680.
My pieces run 21 to 53 words; a new piece stays between 1 and 85.
My pieces run 1 sentence; a new piece has at most 2.
The longest sentence in my pieces runs 21 to 53 words; in a new piece it stays at most 85 words.
At most 24 line breaks: my pieces carry 12 to 18.
No blank lines: none of my pieces has one.
No hashtags: none of my pieces has one.
No mentions (@): none of my pieces has one.
No links: none of my pieces has one.
No emoji: none of my pieces has one.
Open on a claim, as my pieces do.
Close on a statement, as my pieces do.
The first word is a symbol or emoji, as in every piece of mine.
Quoted phrases: about 53.7 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries no more than its length expects.
Colons: about 28.7 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
Figures written in digits: about 20.2 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries no more than its length expects.
Nominalisations (-tion, -ment, -ness, -ity, -ance, -ence): about 8.8 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
Runs of five or more one-syllable words: about 2.9 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
I keep paragraphs to 2 sentences at most.

Write none of the moves that mark text as machine-written (announcing an insight others "miss", grading your own list, "the single most", announcing candour, "that's the whole game", reading the reader's mind, one thing "wearing another's clothes", a contrastive verdict as the opening line, an em dash, a run of three or more very short sentences).
No mechanical errors: spelling, agreement, punctuation.
